lines.text: Welcome to the Lustre Brothers Circus! Mind the wagons, they've got right of way. They've always had right of way.
Down the midway, round the ring, and out of the cannon. Don't worry. I asked about the cannon. They said it's mostly confetti.
The top flap blew open this morning, so that's your way out of the tent. Lionel calls it a feature. I call it a draught.
Ladies and gentlemen, opening night! Oh, no. We're not jumping over the Ferris wheel. That'd be irresponsible. We're going through it.
I used to jump six buses right over there. Seven, according to the posters. We counted the snack wagon. Tonight it's your turn to give these folks a show.
The roller coaster is perfectly safe. It's been tested by professionals. Well, by me. I used to be a professional. Hold on, lean in, and enjoy the fireworks!
A real crowd tonight, folks. Fireworks, string lights, the whole pier lit up. I haven't seen this park this full since my last show. Let's give them something to remember.
Welcome, welcome, one and all! Now, this is just a gentle introductory outing. A little drive, a little float, a little flight, a little dip. I checked every ramp myself. Twice. Mostly.
Folks, a word about the wildlife. The big fellow's a plant eater. Lovely disposition. Now, the other fellow... let's keep moving. Engines on!
Car, boat, plane and submarine. One machine, four ways to have a wonderful afternoon. If it changes shape on you, that means it's working. If it doesn't... keep your elbows in.
This is a private trial, just us and a few curious dinosaurs. Nobody's watching. Which is a shame, because I've got a feeling this is going to be spectacular.
Rae says nobody beats her from the Coral Vault up the waterfall. She says it a lot. Let's find out.
Chip wants a one-on-one over both coasters, all the way to the top hat. He's already booked a camera crew.
Vivi says the cannon is her stage. From the big top's door to the top flap, one on one. She's already practising her bow.
Now that's a show! Head to the Garage, partner. I had them mix you a new paint, on the house.
Not this time, but the show's not over. Lionel's already resetting the ring. Shall we go again?
The cannon takes a little getting used to. My first time, I landed in the popcorn stand. Very tasty.
First place under the big top! Lionel's ringing his bell. Through gritted teeth, but he's ringing it.
A winner! Wagons, the Globe, the cannon and the river. Somebody get that racer a top hat.
On the podium! The elephants approve. One of them sneezed, and I'm taking that as a yes.
Lovely racing! You came out of that cannon like a real pro. Better than me in eighty-seven.
Not this time, but the crowd's still clapping. Opening nights are like that. Shall we go again?
The coaster takes a little getting used to. My first ride, I came off at the top. On purpose. Mostly.
Chin up! Every great show has a rehearsal. That was the rehearsal.
First place on opening night! Listen to that crowd! They haven't cheered like that since 1987.
A winner! Through the wheel, over the gap and under the pier. The posters will need a bigger font.
Now that's a big finish! I may have to give you my nickname. Just borrow it. Just for tonight.
On the podium on opening night! The crowd loved it. So did the octopus, I think.
Lovely racing. You rode that coaster like you were born on it. Were you? No? Well, close enough.
A podium! The fireworks were for you, by the way. And partly for me.
Back of the pack, but you finished, and you finished in one piece. That counts for a lot around here.
Don't you worry. My first stunt, I jumped one bus. Well, into one bus. Try again!
Everybody starts somewhere. I started in a cannon. Let's have another go.
First place! I told everyone this was a gentle outing. You made it look gentle.
A win on the very first trial! Somebody fetch me a bigger poster.
Well, look at that. Not a scratch on the machine, and only a little dinosaur drool. Wonderful!
A podium finish! And all four shapes came back. That's a successful trial in my book.
Very nice driving. The plant eater was very impressed. The other fellow, I didn't ask.
On the podium! See? Gentle introductory outing. Nothing to worry about.
Midway, big top, cannon, river. Have a ball, partner!
Mind the wagons and aim for the top flap!
Opening night, folks! Through the wheel, not over it!
Coaster, flume, sea and pier. Have fun out there!
Gentle introductory outing, folks. Mind the dinosaurs.
Four shapes, one lap. Off you go!
Three stops, three shows, and a tour that's really happening. Thank you, partner. Now, about that volcano...
Well, hello there! You must be one of my racers. Buck Barlow. They call me Big Finish. Long story.
I've had a dream for years, a racing tour where one machine drives, sails, flies and dives, all in one lap.
Before we go public, a private trial. A gentle introductory outing at a lovely little jungle course.
Finish in the top three and the tour's on. Don't mind the dinosaurs. Most of them are vegetarian.
That's it! That's the tour! I knew it! I'm calling the park tonight.
You've earned your spot, partner. Next stop: Coaster Coast, and this time there'll be a crowd.
Not quite the top three. That's all right. The trial's for learning. The dinosaurs will wait.
Take another run at it, and keep an eye on that route strip at the top. It never lies. Unlike my posters.
Coaster Coast. I did my stunt shows on this very pier. The owner still owes me a hot dog.
Tonight it's the tour's public opening. Grandstands, fireworks, the whole town watching.
The route goes up the roller coaster, through the Ferris wheel, down the log flume and under the pier. Perfectly safe.
Top three keeps the tour rolling. No pressure. Well, a little pressure. It's a show!
Listen to them! That's the sound of a tour that's here to stay!
Folks are already asking where we go next. I've got a few ideas. Most of them are probably fine.
Opening nights are tricky. The crowd's still here, the coaster's still running. Let's go again.
Ride the coaster all the way and take the wheel's middle if you dare. You've got this.
The Lustre Brothers Circus. Lionel Lustre and I shared a bill back in eighty-seven. He had elephants. I had a bus.
He's sent a letter. Let me read it. Quote: Buck, old boy, I hear you've gone respectable. Prove you've still got it. Unquote.
So we race his circus! The midway, the Globe of Death, the ring, and the human cannonball, straight out of the top flap.
A top three finish, and I get to send Lionel a letter of my own. I've already written it. It's very short.
Ha! Did you see Lionel's face? I'm framing it. Well, I'm framing the photo. He wouldn't sit still.
He shook my hand, you know. Said we still have it. He said we. I'm choosing to hear it that way.
Not quite the top three. Lionel's being gracious. Very loudly gracious. Let's give him something to be quiet about.
Keep to the middle of the midway, the wagons keep to the sides. And trust the cannon. I mostly do.
A quick safety note: the signs say 'no flying over the crowd'. Somebody fixed my signs again. They used to say 'please'.
When I was your age I jumped a canyon on a lawnmower. Small canyon. Very big lawnmower.
Safety first, folks. That's why I always do the dangerous bits second.
They called me Big Finish because I never once stopped halfway. Started halfway, once or twice.
If anything goes wrong, remember: it's not a crash, it's an unscheduled transformation.
I once raced a hot air balloon across a lake. I won. The balloon was going the other way, but I won.
